html:
Three decisions that mattered most

  1. The assistant is another door into the same room, not a second system. The website and both MCP servers call one function (submit_application) that validates, enforces one live application per mobile and per person, and serialises double submits. The MCP servers contain no scheme rules of their own, so they cannot drift from the counter. Identity is the OAuth token's sub (the OTP-verified mobile): no citizen tool takes a mobile number, so an assistant cannot even name someone else's application.
  2. Two servers, two audiences, two tool sets, and a live sign-in. Each endpoint accepts only tokens minted for its own URL with its own role and scope, and checks on every call that the sign-in has not been ended, so signing out at a kiosk takes effect at once, not 30 minutes later. A citizen's assistant never sees an officer tool.
  3. The assistant proposes; a person disposes, and the server enforces it. Citizen: a preview returns a review token bound to exactly what was read back; submit needs that token and an explicit declaration flag. Officer: a reason is mandatory, hard red flags (under 60, no age proof) make approval impossible, soft ones must be acknowledged by name, one case at a time. Everything an applicant typed is returned under applicant_supplied and treated as data (the poisoned-village eval).

The one I would make differently. The portal has a single shared officer login, so 'recorded against her name' really means officer:admin. With more time I would add named officer accounts and block scoping first, because accountability is what the Director's IT team is really asking for. Close behind: the one-application-per-mobile rule blocks a wife on her husband's phone (the assistant explains and sends her to the counter, and does not work around it).

Not done / limits. The small-model layer ran on one model (Haiku) with scripted follow-ups; the scheme window in config ends 31 Oct 2026 and the nightly job deems all 700 old pending applications approved at start-up (see docs/DEPLOY.md); no rate limiting; the MCP transport is a small hand-written stateless implementation (checked against the official SDK client).
